meta.description: Vane queueing network back-test against documented LV events
meta.run_note: Predicted values from theory-grounded queueing network. Documented values from public sources (after-action reports, media, CTA). No instrument-measured queue data from any LV venue.

events.documented_source: LVMPD After-Action Report; NFL Operations Report; Las Vegas Review-Journal; ESPN coverage 2024-02-11
events.documented_issues: Significant congestion at south gates; VIP entry delays; some attendees queued 45+ minutes at secondary screening checkpoints.
events.documented_notes: Enhanced Super Bowl-level security (far more rigorous than standard NFL). ~115,000 additional people in surrounding corridor (non-ticket holders). Clear weather; no weather-driven service degradation.
events.comparison_notes: [steady-state MC (operational rates)] Predicted P10-P90 interval overlaps the documented range. Known modeling gaps: Super Bowl security protocol is ~2× more thorough than standard NFL — model uses standard NFL service rates (under-predicts wait). | Surrounding 115k non-ticket crowd compresses vehicle/pedestrian access to gates — not modeled; likely explains longer tail in real waits. | VIP/club entry is parallel fast lane — keeps average down vs. general admission.
known_modeling_gaps: Super Bowl security protocol is ~2× more thorough than standard NFL — model uses standard NFL service rates (under-predicts wait).
Surrounding 115k non-ticket crowd compresses vehicle/pedestrian access to gates — not modeled; likely explains longer tail in real waits.
VIP/club entry is parallel fast lane — keeps average down vs. general admission.

top_recommendations: Add 1 lanes at gate 5 to bring modeled utilization toward 82%.
Reduce average wait time (currently 46 min) to improve experience.

events.documented_source: ESPN; MMA Fighting; MMA media pool; attendee social media reports; Sphere venue operational commentary (inaugural event)
events.documented_issues: Some confusion with new venue navigation and entry flow; but operations generally praised as efficient for inaugural event. Heat was a significant attendee concern during exterior queuing.
events.documented_notes: First major sporting event at The Sphere (opened Sept 2023). Capacity 18,600 — near-full house. Enhanced security for inaugural event. Venetian/Palazzo area infrastructure supported access. Unique circular entry geometry not fully captured in model topology.
events.comparison_notes: [steady-state MC (operational rates)] Predicted P10-P90 interval overlaps the documented range. Known modeling gaps: Sphere gate count is low-confidence estimate (not publicly documented). Model may over- or under-estimate entry throughput. | Unique circular entry geometry and Venetian casino integration differ from standard arena topology in model. | Inaugural event: staff learning curve not modeled (adds variance). | Heat stress (100°F) degrades outdoor queuing comfort — weather_factor=0.65 captures service degradation but not attendee patience/behavior change.
known_modeling_gaps: Sphere gate count is low-confidence estimate (not publicly documented). Model may over- or under-estimate entry throughput.
Unique circular entry geometry and Venetian casino integration differ from standard arena topology in model.
Inaugural event: staff learning curve not modeled (adds variance).
Heat stress (100°F) degrades outdoor queuing comfort — weather_factor=0.65 captures service degradation but not attendee patience/behavior change.

top_recommendations: Add 4 lanes at security 3 to bring modeled utilization toward 82%.
Concession operations are efficient. No action needed.
Reduce average wait time (currently 36 min) to improve experience.

events.documented_source: Consumer Technology Association (CTA) official reports; LVCVA attendance data; Las Vegas Review-Journal CES 2024 coverage
events.documented_issues: West Hall to North Hall transit congestion; food court overcrowding at lunch; registration surge at 9–10 AM.
events.documented_notes: Convention pattern: morning surge at registration, sustained lunch-hour congestion at concessions/food, gradual afternoon taper. Registration desks are the primary bottleneck. LVCC has ~200 entry points across multiple halls — model topology aggregates these into gate nodes.
events.comparison_notes: [steady-state MC (operational rates)] Model UNDER-PREDICTS by 10.0-20.0 min. Known modeling gaps: Convention registration desks function differently from stadium gates — badge scanning/printing adds service time not in standard 'ticketing' rates. | LVCC has 200+ entry points across West/Central/North halls; model aggregates into a single gate/security topology. | Convention attendees self-select arrival times heavily; Beta-distribution arrival curve may not capture the registration surge shape. | Lunch-hour concession surge is a distinct second peak not in arrival model.
known_modeling_gaps: Convention registration desks function differently from stadium gates — badge scanning/printing adds service time not in standard 'ticketing' rates.
LVCC has 200+ entry points across West/Central/North halls; model aggregates into a single gate/security topology.
